name: linenoise
listed_description: A small self-contained alternative to readline and libedit.
reason: README (4.4k stars, BSD-2-Clause, last commit 2026-05-02) compares only size and licence: about 1600 lines of code versus readline at 30k lines and libedit at 20k, no runtime, latency, startup or memory numbers. No benchmark directory in the repo (linenoise.c, linenoise-test.c, example.c only) and WebSearch found no third-party speed comparison. It is a line editor, not a lexer, so the guessed category was wrong too.

name: linenoise-ng
listed_description: A small, portable GNU readline replacement for Linux, Windows and MacOS which is capable of handling UTF-8 characters.
reason: README (373 stars, BSD, archived 2020-10-28) lists features, build steps and portability only; no performance, size or memory numbers against readline, libedit or the original linenoise. Repo has include/, src/ and tst/ with no benchmark directory. WebSearch for line-editor benchmarks returned only qualitative descriptions. Line editor, not a lexer, so the guessed category was off.

name: replxx
listed_description: A readline and libedit replacement that supports UTF-8, syntax highlighting, hints, works on Unix and Windows.
reason: README (768 stars, BSD) has features, build and tested-terminal lists only; no speed, latency or size comparison against readline, libedit or linenoise. Root contains examples/, include/, src/ and tests.py with no benchmark directory; master's last commit shown is 2021-11-25. No third-party comparison found by WebSearch. Line editor, not a lexer, so the guessed category was off.

name: PIRE
listed_description: Perl Incompatible Regular Expressions library by Yandex. Can be really fast (more than 400 MB/s).
reason: README and README.ru (337 stars, archived 2025-06-10) give only an absolute figure: 'more than 400 MB/s on our hardware is common', about 5 machine instructions per character, about 10 regexps per pass at the same speed. Hardware is unspecified and no baseline (std::regex, PCRE, RE2, Hyperscan) is named or measured. tools/bench/run-bench and bench.cpp time only PIRE scanners against a null-scanner memory-bandwidth run, with no competing library. WebSearch (English and Russian) found no head-to-head benchmark including PIRE; habr.com is blocked here.
